conclusion: Next-token prediction is not, by itself, a theory of compositional content: finite predictive statistics can agree while the induced quotients compose differently under larger contexts. We study an alternative, non-gradient formulation in which a language model is an audited ledger of finite theory extensions rather than a parameter vector. Six Birds Theory (SBT) supplies the admissibility calculus: typed closure-package layers, explicit quotient maps, audit records, nonclaim records, and promotion gates based on descent, stability, control, no-smuggling, legibility, and strict factorization failure. We introduce Language Theory Models (LTMs), a prototype architecture for structural recovery on fixed sequence corpora. An LTM accumulates typed transition evidence, monitors each active layer with a conditional-information closure-deficit statistic and an idempotence/self-consistency defect, and proposes new layers only when the current quotient leaves recoverable structure unresolved. Candidate layers are committed only after an explicit gate panel emits a strict-extension certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent rather than laundering fallback evidence into a stronger claim. We report a code-backed feasibility study on Shakespeare: the runtime builds closure-package layers, records promotion attempts and failures, emits halt verdicts, caps unaudited fallback readout, and demonstrates strict R-layer growth in bounded runs. Independent of the LTM runtime, we provide a structural probe suite that tests SBT framework-level commitments under blue-team and red-team cases, including growth, forgetting, uncertainty, auditability, and concept-separation scenarios. The contribution is a concrete audited substrate for testing whether compositional structure in a fixed corpus can be recovered as a finite ladder of certified theory refinements.

Relative to next-token and autoregressive language modeling \cite{Bengio2003NPLM,Vaswani2017Attention}, the LTM is not a replacement objective: it adds a non-gradient ledger that audits where a fixed corpus does or does not support compositional refinement claims. Relative to compositional generalization benchmarks such as SCAN, COGS, and CFQ, which usually evaluate trained models post hoc \cite{Hupkes2020Compositionality}, the LTM instruments the recovery process itself and records non-certifying attempts before a finished artifact is declared; relative to mechanistic interpretability and circuits work \cite{Olah2020ZoomIn,Elhage2021Framework,Olsson2022InductionHeads,Conmy2023ACDC}, it shares the auditability motivation but tracks typed recovery layers and gate-panel decisions rather than activation patches or circuit attributions; and relative to symbolic, neurosymbolic, and program-induction approaches \cite{Ellis2023DreamCoder,GarcezLamb2020Neurosymbolic}, it is adjacent in seeking typed structural objects but treats them as recoveries from a fixed corpus with explicit nonclaim records rather than as programs from a search engine.

Three runtime objects carry the measurable status of a candidate layer. The closure-deficit statistic $\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}$ is a conditional-information residual statistic at lookahead $\tau$ that measures unresolved structure under the current quotient \cite{CoverThomas1991Information,Tishby2000Bottleneck}: positive values indicate that recoverable structure remains outside the layer, while values bounded near zero indicate that the quotient is consistent with the corpus at the declared lookahead \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}. The idempotence/self-consistency defect $\delta_{\tau,f}$ is a fixed-point gap for the layer's own quotient map at lookahead $\tau$ through readout $f$, measuring how closely the empirical data satisfy the idempotence relation introduced above \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}. Schematically, the diagnostics separate residual structure from self-consistency:
\[
\mathrm{CD}_{\tau} > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{unresolved structure}, \qquad
\delta_{\tau,f} \approx 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{empirical self-consistency}.
\]
Where \Cref{subsec:audited-layers} states an exact idempotent map, the empirical estimator allows a small positive $\delta_{\tau,f}$ deviation and reports it in the audit log rather than hiding it. The symbol $\mathsf{StrictExtCert}$ denotes the strict-extension certificate, a typed witness object that licenses adding a candidate as a new layer in the ladder \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}. Three runtime objects carry the measurable status of a candidate layer. The closure-deficit statistic $\CDtau$ is a conditional-information residual statistic at lookahead $\tau$ that measures unresolved structure under the current quotient \cite{CoverThomas1991Information,Tishby2000Bottleneck}: positive values indicate that recoverable structure remains outside the layer, while values bounded near zero indicate that the quotient is consistent with the corpus at the declared lookahead \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}. The idempotence/self-consistency defect $\IDef$ is a fixed-point gap for the layer's own quotient map at lookahead $\tau$ through readout $f$, measuring how closely the empirical data satisfy the idempotence relation introduced above \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}. Schematically, the diagnostics separate residual structure from self-consistency:
\[
\CDtau > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{unresolved structure}, \qquad
\IDef \approx 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{empirical self-consistency}.
\]
Where \Cref{subsec:audited-layers} states an exact idempotent map, the empirical estimator allows a small positive $\IDef$ deviation and reports it in the audit log rather than hiding it. The symbol $\strictcert$ denotes the strict-extension certificate, a typed witness object that licenses adding a candidate as a new layer in the ladder \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}. A candidate is committed only after the gate panel emits this certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with the gate mechanics described in \Cref{sec:methods} and formal definitions deferred to \Cref{app:definitions}.

A typed audited layer is a pair
\[
\Tlayer{i}=(\Xspace{i},\opmap{i}),
\]
where \(\Xspace{i}\) is a finite microstate space and \(\opmap{i}:\Xspace{i}\to\Xspace{i}\) is an idempotent self-map,
\[
\opmap{i}\circ\opmap{i}=\opmap{i}.
\]
The induced equivalence relation on \(\Xspace{i}\) identifies two microstates when they lie in the same pre-image of a fixed point in the image of \(\opmap{i}\). Equivalently, the quotient partition is the partition of \(\Xspace{i}\) into fibers of the map onto its fixed-point image \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}.

Schematically, for an observed current microstate \(X_0\) and a future window \(X_{>0,\le \tau}\),
\[
\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}
\;\approx\;
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid \opmap{i}(X_0)\right)
-
H\!\left(X_{>0,\le \tau}\mid X_0\right).
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}\) is the conditional-entropy gap between prediction from the layer quotient and prediction from the raw microstate, restricted to the declared lookahead window.
